intro: `Adobe Photoshop` is a professional image editor used for photo retouching, compositing, digital painting and graphic design. It works with pixels, so you can change every detail of a picture.
It is sold as part of Adobe's Creative Cloud subscription and runs on Windows and macOS, with companion apps on some other devices.

capabilities.title: Layers
capabilities.text: Stack images, text and effects on separate layers so you can change one without touching the rest.

capabilities.title: Selections and masks
capabilities.text: Isolate part of an image and hide or reveal it without deleting anything.

capabilities.title: Adjustment layers
capabilities.text: Change colour, brightness and contrast in a way you can undo or edit later.

capabilities.title: Retouching tools
capabilities.text: Remove blemishes, clone areas and repair damaged photos.

capabilities.title: Smart objects
capabilities.text: Resize and filter images without permanently losing quality.

capabilities.title: Brushes and painting
capabilities.text: Paint and draw with customisable brushes, including pressure-sensitive pen support.

helps: Photoshop helps you turn an ordinary photo into the image you imagined. You can fix lighting, remove distractions, swap backgrounds and combine several pictures into one.
It is also used to prepare artwork for the web, print and social media, with control over size, colour and export.
why: Photoshop has been an industry standard for years, so designers, photographers and agencies often expect files in its format.
It connects with other Adobe apps and a large ecosystem of brushes, plugins and tutorials, which makes it easy to find help for almost any task.

workflows.title: Photo retouching
workflows.text: Adjust exposure and colour, then clean up details with healing and clone tools.

workflows.title: Compositing
workflows.text: Cut out subjects, place them on a new background and blend them with masks.

workflows.title: Social and web graphics
workflows.text: Set up an artboard, add text and shapes, then export for each platform.

workflows.title: Mockups
workflows.text: Place a design inside a product or screen mockup using smart objects.

beyond.purpose: Keep edits and quality when you scale or filter a layer
Hide parts of a layer without erasing them
Record a series of steps and replay them on other images
Edit raw photo files before bringing them in
Fill, extend or change areas of an image from a text description
Save optimised files for web and apps

tips: Use adjustment layers and masks instead of editing pixels directly, so you can go back.
Name and group your layers as you work. Large files get confusing quickly.
Keep a copy of the original photo and save your work as a PSD file.
Learn a few shortcuts for brush size, undo and zoom to move faster.
Features and plans change often, so check Adobe's site for current details.
audience: Photoshop suits photographers, graphic designers, illustrators and marketers who need precise control over images.
It can feel large for a beginner, but you only need a few tools to start, and you can learn more as your projects grow.

intro: `Figma` is a collaborative design tool for user interfaces, prototypes and design systems. It runs in the browser, with a desktop app as well, so designers, developers and managers can open the same file.
Its real-time collaboration, where several people edit at once and see each other's cursors, is what set it apart.

capabilities.title: Vector design
capabilities.text: Draw shapes, icons and layouts with precise vector tools.

capabilities.title: Auto layout
capabilities.text: Make frames that resize and rearrange as content changes.

capabilities.title: Components and variants
capabilities.text: Build reusable pieces, such as buttons, and switch their states easily.

capabilities.title: Prototyping
capabilities.text: Link screens together to create clickable flows you can test.

capabilities.title: Real-time collaboration
capabilities.text: Work in the same file with teammates and leave comments on the design.

capabilities.title: Plugins and widgets
capabilities.text: Extend the tool with community add-ons.

helps: Figma helps teams agree on how a product should look and behave before any code is written. You can draw screens, connect them and share a link for feedback.
It also reduces hand-offs. Developers can inspect spacing, colours and text styles directly in the file.
why: Because it runs in a browser, there is nothing complicated to install, and everyone works on the latest version of a file.
Shared components and styles make it practical to keep a consistent look across a large product.

workflows.title: Design a screen
workflows.text: Start with a frame, add layout, text and components, then refine the spacing.

workflows.title: Build a design system
workflows.text: Create colour, text styles and components and publish them as a shared library.

workflows.title: Prototype a flow
workflows.text: Connect frames with interactions and share a link to test the idea.

workflows.title: Hand off to developers
workflows.text: Developers inspect measurements and export assets from the same file.

beyond.purpose: Make designs that adapt to content and screen size
Store values such as colours and spacing for reuse and theming
Give developers inspection tools and specs
Run brainstorms and workshops on an online whiteboard
Add features such as icon libraries and content fillers
Go back to an earlier state of the file

tips: Use components for anything you repeat, so one change updates every copy.
Name layers and frames clearly, because developers will read them.
Learn auto layout early. It saves a lot of manual resizing.
Share a view-only link when you want feedback without risking edits.
Plans and limits change, so check Figma's site for current details.
audience: Figma suits UI and UX designers, product teams, developers and students who work on apps and websites.
It is a good place to start because the free plan lets you learn the tool with real projects.

intro: `GIMP` stands for GNU Image Manipulation Program. It is a free, open-source image editor for photo retouching, compositing and illustration, available on Windows, macOS and Linux.
Many people use it as a no-cost alternative to paid editors, and it can handle a wide range of everyday and advanced image tasks.

capabilities.title: Layers and masks
capabilities.text: Combine images and control what shows with layer masks.

capabilities.title: Selection tools
capabilities.text: Choose areas by shape, colour or freehand outline.

capabilities.title: Retouching
capabilities.text: Clone, heal and sharpen parts of a photo.

capabilities.title: Colour tools
capabilities.text: Adjust levels, curves, hue and saturation.

capabilities.title: Filters and effects
capabilities.text: Apply blurs, distortions and many other effects.

capabilities.title: Scripting and plug-ins
capabilities.text: Automate work and add features through scripts and extensions.

helps: GIMP helps you edit photos and make images without paying for software. You can crop and resize, fix colours, remove objects and build graphics for the web.
Because it is open source, the community adds plug-ins, brushes and tutorials that extend what it can do.
why: GIMP is free to use and modify, and it works across operating systems, which makes it popular with students, hobbyists and Linux users.
It reads and writes many file formats, including Photoshop's PSD files in many cases, so it fits into mixed workflows.

workflows.title: Fix a photo
workflows.text: Crop, straighten, correct colour and sharpen before exporting.

workflows.title: Remove an object
workflows.text: Select it and use healing or clone tools to fill the space.

workflows.title: Make a web banner
workflows.text: Create a new image, add layers for text and shapes, and export a compressed file.

workflows.title: Batch edits
workflows.text: Use scripts or plug-ins to resize or convert many images.

beyond.purpose: Draw precise curves and turn them into selections
Blend layers in different ways
Automate repeated work with scripts
Add extra tools from the community
Save layered files so you can keep editing later
Arrange docks and tools to suit your work

tips: Save a layered XCF copy while you work, and export JPG or PNG only at the end.
Duplicate a layer before experimenting so you can compare results.
Use layer masks instead of the eraser, so you can undo changes later.
Check the official site for the current version and its newest features.
Look for community tutorials when you want a particular effect.
audience: GIMP suits students, hobbyists, bloggers, small businesses and anyone who needs a capable image editor at no cost.
It takes some time to learn, but it rewards you with plenty of control.

intro: `Inkscape` is a free, open-source vector graphics editor. Instead of pixels, it stores shapes and paths, so drawings stay sharp at any size, from a small icon to a large poster.
Its main file format is SVG, an open standard that works well on the web.

capabilities.title: Vector drawing
capabilities.text: Draw shapes and curves with Bezier tools and edit every node.

capabilities.title: Text on paths
capabilities.text: Set type along a curve or inside a shape.

capabilities.title: Trace bitmap
capabilities.text: Turn a raster picture into editable vector paths.

capabilities.title: Path operations
capabilities.text: Combine, subtract and intersect shapes to build new ones.

capabilities.title: Gradients and patterns
capabilities.text: Fill shapes with colour blends and repeating patterns.

capabilities.title: Extensions
capabilities.text: Add features through built-in and community extensions.

helps: Inkscape helps you make artwork that must scale cleanly, such as logos, icons, diagrams and illustrations.
It is also useful for preparing designs for printing, cutting machines and web graphics.
why: Inkscape gives you professional vector tools without a licence fee, and SVG is an open format, so your work is not locked to one program.
It runs on Windows, macOS and Linux, and a helpful community shares tutorials and extensions.

workflows.title: Design a logo
workflows.text: Sketch with basic shapes, refine the nodes and export it in several sizes.

workflows.title: Make an icon set
workflows.text: Draw icons on a grid and export each one as SVG or PNG.

workflows.title: Vectorise a sketch
workflows.text: Scan a drawing and use Trace Bitmap to turn it into paths.

workflows.title: Prepare for cutting or print
workflows.text: Convert text to paths and organise colours before exporting.

beyond.purpose: Adjust the points and handles that define a curve
Apply live, editable changes to a path
Make linked copies that update with the original
Organise complex drawings
Convert drawings to PNG or PDF from scripts
Add tools for specific jobs

tips: Keep shapes simple and use as few nodes as you can for smooth curves.
Convert text to paths before sending a file to someone who may not have your fonts.
Use layers and clear names for anything with many parts.
Learn the shortcuts for the selection, node and shape tools.
Save your working file as Inkscape SVG, and export other formats only at the end.
audience: Inkscape suits graphic designers, illustrators, students, makers and anyone who needs scalable artwork without a paid licence.
It is also a good fit for technical diagrams and web graphics.

intro: `Krita` is a free, open-source painting program made for digital artists. It is built around drawing and illustration, with a large set of brushes and tools for pen tablets.
It runs on Windows, macOS and Linux, and its native file format is KRA.

capabilities.title: Brush engines
capabilities.text: Choose from many brush types and tune them to your style.

capabilities.title: Stabilisers
capabilities.text: Smooth shaky lines so your strokes look cleaner.

capabilities.title: Layers and masks
capabilities.text: Paint on separate layers, with masks and blend modes.

capabilities.title: Drawing assistants
capabilities.text: Use guides for perspective, symmetry and straight lines.

capabilities.title: Animation tools
capabilities.text: Make frame-by-frame animation on a timeline.

capabilities.title: Colour management
capabilities.text: Work with several colour spaces for screen or print.

helps: Krita helps you paint, sketch and ink comics, concept art and illustrations on a computer without buying software.
Its tools are tuned for drawing, so it feels closer to traditional media than a general photo editor does.
why: Artists like Krita because it is free, focused on painting and developed with input from working illustrators.
Its resource system lets you share and install brushes, patterns and templates made by others.

workflows.title: Concept art
workflows.text: Block in shapes with a large brush, then refine the details on new layers.

workflows.title: Comics and manga
workflows.text: Use panel templates, ink on a separate layer and add tone.

workflows.title: Digital painting
workflows.text: Sketch, colour and finish with custom brushes and blend modes.

workflows.title: Simple animation
workflows.text: Draw frames on the timeline and play them back.

beyond.purpose: Save and share brushes that suit your style
Paint seamless, repeating textures
Apply adjustments you can edit later
Pick brushes and colours quickly while you draw
Create and edit frame animation
Automate tasks and add tools

tips: Connect a drawing tablet if you can, since many features are designed for pen pressure.
Put sketch, colour and lines on different layers so you can change one at a time.
Try a few brush presets before building your own.
Turn on a stabiliser for clean line work.
Save in KRA to keep layers, and export PNG or JPG for sharing.
audience: Krita suits illustrators, concept artists, comic creators, animators and anyone learning digital painting.
It is a strong choice if you want a free, art-focused program rather than a general photo editor.
